text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.66% today to close at $393.52, continuing a recovery from a sharp four-day drop that saw the stock fall nearly 9% from mid-September. The modest gain reflects choppy sentiment around oil markets: crude prices remain volatile as geopolitical tension between the U.S. and Iran swings between escalation (Trump rejecting Iran's ceasefire proposal) and de-escalation (recent UN talks), creating uncertainty for refiners about future energy supply and margins.

The refining backdrop is mixed. U.S. refineries are running at 94% capacity with healthy fuel stocks (gasoline and diesel both well-stocked), which generally limits upside for refiner profits. However, the 18-point spread between world oil ($114.89/barrel) and U.S. crude ($96.41/barrel) — a notably wide gap — could still support margins if Marathon can arbitrage the difference through imports, though geopolitical risk on Middle Eastern supply remains a wildcard keeping investors cautious.
